newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - April 23.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - April 23.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors affecting Indian stock markets on Wednesday morning:

** Indian Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral won a vote of confidence in parliament on Tuesday after an ominous warning by the Congress party, his key ally, to keep it happy for the remaining four years of his tenure.
Gujral's victory had been expected after the ruling United Front patched up with its key Congress ally.
** Indian blue chips ended a shade higher on Tuesday, as most action centred around Reliance Industries, which released its annual results, traders said.
** Bombay's benchmark 30-share index ended 0.84 points higher at 3,800.63, off the intra-day high of 3,839.54.
** Indian petrochemicals giant Reliance Industries Ltd on Tuesday announced modestly higher profit for 1996/97 (April-March) and analysts said they foresaw robust earnings in the current year.
Net profit rose to 13.23 billion rupees from 13.05 billion in 1995/96 on higher sales of 87.3 billion rupees against 77.86 billion a year ago.
On the Bombay Stock Exchange, the Reliance share ended 0.25 rupees higher at 308, off 320.25 high -- and after rising 19 percent in the last one week.
The Reliance stock enters a no-delivery period in the new National Stock Exchange account from Wednesday.

** Shares of India's largest aluminium maker National Aluminium Company Ltd (NALCO) ended two rupees, or nearly four percent, lower at 50 rupees at the Bombay exchange on Tuesday after the firm announced a fall in its net profit.
NALCO on Tuesday said its net profit during 1996/97 (April-March) dropped to 4.79 billion rupees, from 5.35 billion a year earlier.
** Hindalco Industries, an Aditya Birla group company is launching a $48 million external commercial borrowing (ECB) transaction, the Economic Times reports.
The issue is being arranged by ANZ Grindlays Bank and Citibank, the paper said. It quoted sources as saying the ECB tranche comprises an infrastructure component along with corporate expansion.
